mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 4.0% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy easing supports risk asset performance.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals economic deterioration, triggering negative equity returns as corporate earnings face demand contraction and profit margin pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over 1 month indicate weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns as earnings growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS occurs in more than 50% of instances where 20-day SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 325 signals persistent inflation, prompting central bank tightening that reduces equity valuations through higher discount rates and earnings uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 325.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above 100.0 indicates robust manufacturing output, driving positive equity returns through sustained corporate profitability and economic expansion.
failure_condition: Rank IC between INDPRO and 60-day SPX returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL rising above 325 within 1 month signals accelerating inflation, triggering negative equity returns as central bank rate hikes increase cost of capital and reduce risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises above 325.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 4.0% indicates labor market tightness, increasing inflation risks and prompting aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and declines in UNRATE signal aggressive monetary tightening during labor market strength, causing negative equity returns through reduced liquidity and earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling occurs in more than 50% of instances where 20-day SPX returns are positive.
